newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila must probe "foreign" hand on peso - senator.
newsitem.headline: Manila must probe "foreign" hand on peso - senator.

text.p: Philippine Senate president Ernesto Maceda on Friday urged the Central Bank to monitor alleged attempts by "foreign forces" to manipulate and weaken the peso.
Maceda, who belongs to the political opposition, issued the call in a statement after the Central Bank widened the peso's trading band, effectively devaluing it 11.5 percent.
Maceda called on the Central Bank "to closely monitor reports that foreign forces are allegedly manipulating the foreign exchange market in the Philippines, in a bid to weaken the Philippine peso."

"Unless corrected, the manipulation of the foreign exchange market could lead to the drastic rise in inflation rate which, in turn, could lead to radical increase in prices of commodities, to the detriment of low-income families," he said.
Maceda did not say what reports he based his statement on and did not identify who the supposed "foreign forces" were.
Earlier this week, President Fidel Ramos suggested "outsiders" might be behind the pressure on the peso in recent days.
